A simpler rewrite of `docs/original/bone_marrowaging.qmd`, with the fixes
from the pipeline review folded in. Each change from the original is marked
**Changed:** where it happens.

**What the design can and cannot say.** Each sex is one 10x library, so every
male-vs-female number is also a library-vs-library number. Ages are hashed
*within* a library, so age comparisons within a sex are free of batch. Each
age is one hashtag pooling six mice: cells are pseudoreplicates, so p-values
and intervals describe these pools of cells, not variation between mice. Read
the results as hypotheses for per-mouse validation.

# 1. Load and QC each library

The same steps as the original male and female sections, written once and run
for each sex.

```{r}
load_sample <- function(sex) {
  sample_id <- samples[[sex]]
  raw_data      <- Read10X(file.path(data_dir, sample_id, "sample_raw_feature_bc_matrix"))
  filtered_data <- Read10X(file.path(data_dir, sample_id, "sample_filtered_feature_bc_matrix"))

  raw_gex      <- raw_data$`Gene Expression`
  filtered_gex <- filtered_data$`Gene Expression`

  # Explicit zero-pad instead of intersect
  missing_genes <- setdiff(rownames(raw_gex), rownames(filtered_gex))
  if (length(missing_genes) > 0) {
    pad <- Matrix(0, nrow = length(missing_genes), ncol = ncol(filtered_gex), sparse = TRUE,
                  dimnames = list(missing_genes, colnames(filtered_gex)))
    filtered_gex <- rbind(filtered_gex, pad)
  }
  filtered_gex <- filtered_gex[rownames(raw_gex), ]

  # SoupX ambient correction, with a quick clustering to satisfy its requirement
  sc <- SoupChannel(tod = raw_gex, toc = filtered_gex, channelName = sample_id)
  quick <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = filtered_gex)
  quick <- NormalizeData(quick, verbose = FALSE)
  quick <- FindVariableFeatures(quick, verbose = FALSE)
  quick <- ScaleData(quick, verbose = FALSE)
  quick <- RunPCA(quick, npcs = 30, verbose = FALSE)
  quick <- FindNeighbors(quick, dims = 1:30, verbose = FALSE)
  quick <- FindClusters(quick, resolution = 0.5, verbose = FALSE)
  sc <- setClusters(sc, setNames(as.character(quick$seurat_clusters), colnames(quick)))
  sc <- autoEstCont(sc)
  message(sex, ": ", round(100 * sc$fit$rhoEst, 1), "% of counts estimated ambient")

  # Changed: the object is built from the SoupX-ADJUSTED counts. The original
  # computed them (soup_male_bm) but built male_bm from filtered_gex.
  obj <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = adjustCounts(sc, roundToInt = TRUE), project = sample_id)
  obj$sex <- sex

  # ADT: log1p, minus each cell's median isotype signal
  adt <- filtered_data$`Antibody Capture`[, colnames(obj)]
  hto_features     <- names(hto_to_age)
  adt_features     <- setdiff(rownames(adt), hto_features)
  isotype_features <- grep("^Isotype", adt_features, value = TRUE)
  adt_log <- log1p(as.matrix(adt[adt_features, ]))
  adt_centred <- sweep(adt_log, 2, colMedians(adt_log[isotype_features, , drop = FALSE]), "-")

  obj[["ADT"]] <- CreateAssayObject(counts = adt[adt_features, ])
  obj[["ADT"]]$data <- adt_centred
  obj[["HTO"]] <- CreateAssayObject(counts = adt[hto_features, ])

  # Hashtags -> age
  obj <- NormalizeData(obj, assay = "HTO", normalization.method = "CLR", margin = 2)
  obj <- MULTIseqDemux(obj, assay = "HTO", autoThresh = TRUE)
  obj$MULTI_ID <- as.character(obj$MULTI_ID)
  obj$age <- unname(hto_to_age[obj$MULTI_ID])
  obj$age_sex <- paste0(obj$age, "_", toupper(substr(sex, 1, 1)))

  # QC metrics
  obj$log10GenesPerUMI <- log10(obj$nFeature_RNA) / log10(obj$nCount_RNA)
  obj$mitoRatio <- PercentageFeatureSet(obj, pattern = "^mt-") / 100
  obj$riboRatio <- PercentageFeatureSet(obj, pattern = "^Rp[sl]") / 100
  obj$percent.hb <- PercentageFeatureSet(obj, features = grep("^(Hba|Hbb)", rownames(obj), value = TRUE))

  # Doublets, per hashtag group
  sce <- SingleCellExperiment(list(counts = LayerData(obj, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")))
  sce <- scDblFinder(sce, samples = obj$MULTI_ID)
  obj$scDblFinder.class <- sce$scDblFinder.class
  obj
}

bm <- lapply(names(samples), load_sample)
names(bm) <- names(samples)
```

```{r}
VlnPlot(bm$male, features = c("log10GenesPerUMI", "mitoRatio", "percent.hb"), group.by = "age")
VlnPlot(bm$female, features = c("log10GenesPerUMI", "mitoRatio", "percent.hb"), group.by = "age")
```

**Changed: QC thresholds are set per library by median absolute deviation**,
not one fixed cutoff. Mature neutrophils carry the least RNA, so a fixed
cutoff removes them first, and removes more from the shallower library.
Every cell gets a `qc_status` saying why it was kept or removed, and the
surface protein of every hashtagged cell is kept *before* filtering: section 4
uses it to check whether QC, rather than ageing, removed mature cells.

```{r}
qc_status <- function(obj) {
  status <- rep("pass", ncol(obj))
  status[!obj$MULTI_ID %in% names(hto_to_age)] <- "no sample hashtag"
  status[status == "pass" & obj$scDblFinder.class != "singlet"] <- "doublet"

  singlet <- status == "pass"
  sce <- SingleCellExperiment(list(counts = LayerData(obj, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")[, singlet]))
  outlier <- perCellQCFilters(perCellQCMetrics(sce), nmads = 3)$discard
  status[which(singlet)[outlier]] <- "RNA QC: count/feature outlier"
  status[status == "pass" & !(obj$mitoRatio < 0.2)] <- "RNA QC: mitochondrial"
  status[status == "pass" & !(obj$percent.hb < 10)] <- "RNA QC: haemoglobin"
  status
}

protein_preqc <- list()
for (sex in names(bm)) {
  bm[[sex]]$qc_status <- qc_status(bm[[sex]])
  print(table(bm[[sex]]$qc_status))

  hashtagged <- bm[[sex]]$qc_status != "no sample hashtag"
  protein_preqc[[sex]] <- data.frame(
    barcode = colnames(bm[[sex]])[hashtagged],
    sex = sex,
    age = bm[[sex]]$age[hashtagged],
    qc_status = bm[[sex]]$qc_status[hashtagged],
    t(as.matrix(LayerData(bm[[sex]], assay = "ADT", layer = "data")[, hashtagged])),
    check.names = FALSE)

  bm[[sex]] <- subset(bm[[sex]], cells = colnames(bm[[sex]])[bm[[sex]]$qc_status == "pass"])
  message(sex, ": ", ncol(bm[[sex]]), " cells pass QC")
}
saveRDS(protein_preqc, file.path(out_dir, "protein_preqc.rds"))
```

# 3. Merge, stage the granulocytes, match depth

```{r}
# add.cell.ids stops barcodes shared by the two libraries from colliding
bm_merge <- merge(bm$female, bm$male, add.cell.ids = c("female", "male"), merge.data = TRUE)
bm_merge <- JoinLayers(bm_merge, assay = "RNA")
bm_merge <- NormalizeData(bm_merge)
bm_merge <- FindVariableFeatures(bm_merge)
bm_merge <- ScaleData(bm_merge, features = VariableFeatures(bm_merge))
bm_merge <- RunPCA(bm_merge)
bm_merge <- RunUMAP(bm_merge, dims = 1:15)
DimPlot(bm_merge, group.by = "sex", split.by = "age")

gmp_neu <- subset(bm_merge, fine_label_readable %in% c("GMP", "Neutrophils"))
gmp_neu <- FindVariableFeatures(gmp_neu)
gmp_neu <- ScaleData(gmp_neu, features = VariableFeatures(gmp_neu))
gmp_neu <- RunPCA(gmp_neu)
gmp_neu <- RunUMAP(gmp_neu, dims = 1:15)
```

**Changed: stage comes from rank-based marker scores (UCell), not a hand-made
cluster-to-stage map.** The cluster map had to be redone every time cluster
numbering changed, and proNeu2 is merged into proNeu (its markers overlap
proNeu and preNeu almost completely; only 3 of 4512 cells were called proNeu2).

```{r}
stage_signatures <- list(
  GMPs     = c("Elane", "Mpo", "Prtn3", "Ctsg", "Ms4a3", "Kit", "Cd34"),
  proNeu   = c("Elane", "Mpo", "Prtn3", "Ctsg", "Cebpe", "Gfi1", "Fcnb", "Il5ra"),
  preNeu   = c("Ltf", "Camp", "Ngp", "Lcn2", "Chil3", "Fcnb", "Mki67"),
  immature = c("Ltf", "Camp", "Lcn2", "Mmp8", "Cd177", "Ifitm1", "Chil3"),
  mature   = c("Cxcr2", "Sell", "Il1b", "Csf3r", "Mmp9", "S100a8", "S100a9", "Retnlg", "Fpr1")
)
gmp_neu <- AddModuleScore_UCell(gmp_neu, features = stage_signatures, name = "_stage")
stage_scores <- as.matrix(gmp_neu@meta.data[, paste0(stages, "_stage")])
gmp_neu$stage <- factor(stages[max.col(stage_scores, ties.method = "first")], levels = stages)

DimPlot(gmp_neu, group.by = "stage", cols = stage_cols) +
  DimPlot(gmp_neu, group.by = "sex", cols = sex_cols)
table(gmp_neu$stage, gmp_neu$sex)
```

**Changed: depth matching inside each stage.** The libraries differ several-fold
in depth, and mature neutrophils are shallow by nature. Thinning every cell
toward one global target left the shallow cells untouched (male mature cells
sat at 330-590 UMIs against a 2225 target), so their comparisons ran on counts
several-fold apart. Here each stratum is thinned toward its own shallowest
group:

* `RNAmatched`: ages equalised within each sex x stage, for age comparisons.
* `RNAmatched_sex`: every age x sex group equalised within each stage, for
  anything that compares the two libraries.

```{r}
downsample_within <- function(counts, groups, strata) {
  totals <- colSums(counts)
  prop <- rep(1, ncol(counts))
  for (st in unique(strata)) {
    idx <- which(strata == st)
    sizes <- table(groups[idx])
    big <- names(sizes)[sizes >= min_cells]
    if (!length(big)) big <- names(sizes)
    target <- min(sapply(big, function(g) median(totals[idx][groups[idx] == g])))
    prop[idx] <- pmin(1, target / pmax(totals[idx], 1))
  }
  downsampleMatrix(counts, prop = prop, bycol = TRUE)
}

counts <- LayerData(gmp_neu, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
gmp_neu[["RNAmatched"]] <- CreateAssayObject(
  counts = downsample_within(counts, gmp_neu$age, paste(gmp_neu$sex, gmp_neu$stage)))
gmp_neu[["RNAmatched_sex"]] <- CreateAssayObject(
  counts = downsample_within(counts, gmp_neu$age_sex, as.character(gmp_neu$stage)))
gmp_neu <- NormalizeData(gmp_neu, assay = "RNAmatched")
gmp_neu <- NormalizeData(gmp_neu, assay = "RNAmatched_sex")
DefaultAssay(gmp_neu) <- "RNA"

# Median UMIs per stage x sex x age, before and after
depth <- gmp_neu@meta.data |>
  mutate(raw = colSums(counts),
         matched = colSums(LayerData(gmp_neu, assay = "RNAmatched", layer = "counts"))) |>
  group_by(stage, sex, age) |>
  summarise(n = n(), median_umi_raw = median(raw), median_umi_matched = median(matched), .groups = "drop")
depth
```

CytoTRACE2 potency, scored on the matched counts (it reads transcriptional
complexity, so it is the measure most exposed to depth):

```{r}
potency <- cytotrace2(as.matrix(LayerData(gmp_neu, assay = "RNAmatched", layer = "counts")),
                      is_seurat = FALSE, species = "mouse")
gmp_neu <- AddMetaData(gmp_neu, potency)
saveRDS(gmp_neu, file.path(out_dir, "gmp_neutrophils.rds"))
```

# 4. Does the stage mix change with age?

The most direct reading of "how does neutrophil development change with age".
Composition within a sex is batch-free: all ages share the library.

```{r}
wilson <- function(x, n, z = 1.96) {
  p <- x / n; d <- 1 + z^2 / n
  centre <- (p + z^2 / (2 * n)) / d
  half <- z * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2)) / d
  data.frame(ci_low = pmax(0, centre - half), ci_high = pmin(1, centre + half))
}

composition_table <- function(stage, age, sex, levels) {
  df <- data.frame(stage = factor(stage, levels = levels), age = factor(age, levels = ages),
                   sex = sex) |> na.omit() |>
    count(sex, age, stage, .drop = FALSE) |>
    group_by(sex, age) |> mutate(n_group = sum(n), proportion = n / n_group) |> ungroup()
  cbind(df, wilson(df$n, df$n_group))
}

# Log-odds change in a stage's share per age step, from a binomial GLM.
# Changed: this test existed in the pipeline but never ran (it looped over
# levels() of a character column, which is NULL).
composition_trends <- function(comp) {
  comp |> group_by(sex, stage) |> filter(sum(n) >= 20) |>
    group_modify(function(d, key) {
      fit <- glm(cbind(n, n_group - n) ~ as.integer(age), family = binomial, data = d)
      data.frame(prop_first = d$proportion[1], prop_last = d$proportion[nrow(d)],
                 log_odds_per_step = coef(fit)[2],
                 p_value = coef(summary(fit))[2, 4])
    }) |> ungroup() |> group_by(sex) |> mutate(padj = p.adjust(p_value, "BH")) |> ungroup()
}

stage_comp <- composition_table(gmp_neu$stage, gmp_neu$age, gmp_neu$sex, stages)
stage_trends <- composition_trends(stage_comp)
write.csv(stage_comp, file.path(out_dir, "stage_composition.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(stage_trends, file.path(out_dir, "stage_age_trends.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
stage_trends

p <- ggplot(stage_comp, aes(age, proportion, fill = stage)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, colour = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ sex) + scale_fill_manual(values = stage_cols) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of staged cells", title = "Maturation stage mix by age")
p; save_plot(p, "stage_composition", 9, 5)

p <- ggplot(stage_comp, aes(age, proportion, colour = sex, group = sex)) +
  geom_line() + geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high), size = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ stage, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) + scale_colour_manual(values = sex_cols) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of staged cells", caption = "Wilson intervals on cells, not mice")
p; save_plot(p, "stage_trends", 13, 4)
```

# 5. Protein gate: did RNA QC remove the mature cells?

**New.** The male library loses immature and mature cells with age, and those
are the lowest-RNA cells, so the trend could be RNA QC removing aged mature
neutrophils. Surface protein does not depend on RNA capture. Every hashtagged
singlet (QC failures included) is staged by Ly6G / CD11b / CXCR2, with
thresholds set per library (each was stained separately). If protein-defined
mature cells are there before QC and missing after it, the RNA trend is QC loss.

```{r}
# A positive threshold: the density valley between two modes when the marker
# is bimodal, otherwise the 99th percentile of the isotype controls.
valley <- function(x) {
  d <- density(x[is.finite(x)], n = 512)
  peaks <- which(diff(sign(diff(d$y))) == -2) + 1
  peaks <- peaks[order(-d$y[peaks])][1:2]
  if (anyNA(peaks) || abs(diff(d$x[peaks])) < 0.5) return(NA)
  lo <- min(peaks); hi <- max(peaks)
  v <- lo - 1 + which.min(d$y[lo:hi])
  if (d$y[v] > 0.8 * min(d$y[peaks])) NA else d$x[v]
}
threshold <- function(x, background) {
  v <- valley(x)
  if (is.finite(v) && v > background) v else background
}
find_marker <- function(df, pattern) grep(pattern, names(df), value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)[1]

gate_library <- function(df) {
  df <- df[df$qc_status != "doublet", ]
  iso <- grep("^Isotype", names(df), value = TRUE)
  background <- quantile(as.matrix(df[, iso]), 0.99)
  ly6g  <- df[[find_marker(df, "Ly.?6G")]]
  cd11b <- df[[find_marker(df, "CD11b")]]
  cxcr2 <- df[[find_marker(df, "CXCR2|CD182")]]
  if (is.null(ly6g) || is.null(cd11b) || is.null(cxcr2))
    stop("the protein gate needs Ly6G, CD11b and CXCR2 on the panel")

  t_cd11b <- threshold(cd11b, background)
  myeloid <- cd11b > t_cd11b
  t_ly6g <- threshold(ly6g[myeloid], background)
  t_cxcr2 <- threshold(cxcr2[myeloid & ly6g > t_ly6g], background)
  message(df$sex[1], ": thresholds CD11b ", round(t_cd11b, 2), ", Ly6G ",
          round(t_ly6g, 2), ", CXCR2 ", round(t_cxcr2, 2))

  df$protein_stage <- ifelse(!myeloid, NA,
                      ifelse(ly6g <= t_ly6g, "Ly6G- precursor",
                      ifelse(cxcr2 <= t_cxcr2, "Ly6G+ CXCR2- (immature-like)",
                             "Ly6G+ CXCR2+ (mature-like)")))
  df$passed_qc <- df$qc_status == "pass"
  df
}

protein_stages <- c("Ly6G- precursor", "Ly6G+ CXCR2- (immature-like)", "Ly6G+ CXCR2+ (mature-like)")
gated <- bind_rows(lapply(protein_preqc, gate_library)) |> filter(!is.na(protein_stage))

# How much of each protein-defined stage RNA QC kept, per age
retention <- gated |> group_by(sex, protein_stage, age) |>
  summarise(n_before_qc = n(), n_passed = sum(passed_qc), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(retained = n_passed / n_before_qc, age = factor(age, levels = ages))
retention <- cbind(retention, wilson(retention$n_passed, retention$n_before_qc))
write.csv(retention, file.path(out_dir, "protein_gate_retention.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

protein_comp <- bind_rows(
  composition_table(gated$protein_stage, gated$age, gated$sex, protein_stages) |>
    mutate(cells = "before RNA QC"),
  with(gated[gated$passed_qc, ], composition_table(protein_stage, age, sex, protein_stages)) |>
    mutate(cells = "after RNA QC"))
protein_trends <- protein_comp |> group_by(cells) |> group_modify(~ composition_trends(.x))
write.csv(protein_trends, file.path(out_dir, "protein_stage_age_trends.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
protein_trends

p <- ggplot(retention, aes(age, retained, colour = sex, group = sex)) +
  geom_line() + geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high), size = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ protein_stage) + scale_colour_manual(values = sex_cols) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Kept by RNA QC",

       subtitle = "A fall with age in one library means QC, not the marrow, removed those cells")

p <- ggplot(protein_comp, aes(factor(age, levels = ages), proportion, fill = stage)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, colour = "white") + facet_grid(cells ~ sex) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = unname(stage_cols[c(1, 3, 5)])) +
```

# 6. Upstream: the progenitor compartment

Where does a shift in granulopoiesis start? Composition of the SingleR-labelled
progenitors, as each population's share at one age over its share across all
ages of the same library (log2 observed / expected; 0 = as expected).

```{r}
prog <- subset(bm_merge, fine_label_readable %in% progenitors)
prog_comp <- composition_table(prog$fine_label_readable, prog$age, prog$sex, progenitors) |>
  group_by(sex, stage) |>
  mutate(expected = sum(n) / sum(n_group),
         log2_obs_exp = log2((n + 0.5) / (n_group * expected + 0.5))) |>
  ungroup() |> filter(sum(n) >= 20, .by = c(sex, stage))
write.csv(prog_comp, file.path(out_dir, "progenitor_composition.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

p <- ggplot(prog_comp, aes(log2_obs_exp, stage, colour = sex)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ age, nrow = 1) + scale_colour_manual(values = sex_cols) +
  labs(x = "log2(observed / expected share)", y = NULL,
       title = "Progenitor populations over- and under-represented by age")
p; save_plot(p, "progenitor_imbalance", 12, 5)
```

# 7. Where cells sit along the trajectory

One monocle3 trajectory over both sexes, on the matched counts, rooted at the
GMPs programmatically (no Shiny window). **Changed:** the per-age trajectories
and their Venn of "genes unique to each age" are dropped: the ages differ
several-fold in cell number, so that comparison mostly measured power.

```{r}
cds <- new_cell_data_set(
  LayerData(gmp_neu, assay = "RNAmatched", layer = "counts"),
  cell_metadata = gmp_neu@meta.data,
```

Each age against 3m within a sex: the median shift, the share of cells past
the 3m median (0.5 = no shift), and a KS test. Run pooled over stages and
within each stage. **Changed:** the within-stage version gates cell counts per
sex *and* per age (it had pooled the sexes, so male mature at 9m, 20 cells,
was compared).

```{r}
shift_vs_3m <- function(value, meta) {
  rows <- list()
  for (st in c("all stages", stages)) for (sx in names(sex_cols)) {
    keep <- meta$sex == sx & is.finite(value) & (st == "all stages" | meta$stage == st)
    n_age <- table(factor(meta$age[keep], levels = ages))
    if (n_age["3m"] < min_cells) next
    ref <- value[keep & meta$age == "3m"]
    for (a in setdiff(names(n_age)[n_age >= min_cells], "3m")) {
      v <- value[keep & meta$age == a]
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        stage = st, sex = sx, age = a, n = length(v),
        median_shift = median(v) - median(ref),
        frac_beyond_3m_median = mean(v > median(ref)),
        ks_p = suppressWarnings(ks.test(v, ref)$p.value))
    }
  }
  bind_rows(rows) |> mutate(stage = factor(stage, levels = c("all stages", stages)))
}

shifts <- bind_rows(
  shift_vs_3m(gmp_neu$pseudotime, gmp_neu@meta.data) |> mutate(measure = "pseudotime"),
  shift_vs_3m(gmp_neu$CytoTRACE2_Score, gmp_neu@meta.data) |> mutate(measure = "potency"))
write.csv(shifts, file.path(out_dir, "pseudotime_potency_shifts.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

p <- ggplot(shifts, aes(frac_beyond_3m_median, factor(age, levels = ages), colour = sex)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(size = n), position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  facet_grid(measure ~ stage) + scale_colour_manual(values = sex_cols) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Share of cells past the 3m median", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "Pooled shift with flat within-stage panels = the stage mix moving, not the cells")
p; save_plot(p, "pseudotime_potency_shifts", 13, 5)
```

# 8. What changes between 3m and 18m, and do 9m and 12m follow?

Genes are found at the extremes, where cells are most numerous, with a
permutation threshold at 10% FDR; 9m and 12m are then read off for the same
genes as a shape check. Run within each stage and sex, on `RNAmatched`, and
also on surface protein (ADT), the depth-robust readout.

```{r}
endpoint_contrast <- function(expr, age, min_detected = 10, target_fdr = 0.10) {
  keep_cells <- age %in% c("3m", "18m")
  expr <- expr[rowSums(expr[, keep_cells] > 0) >= min_detected, , drop = FALSE]
  effect_of <- function(lab) rowMeans(expr[, keep_cells][, lab == "18m", drop = FALSE]) -
                             rowMeans(expr[, keep_cells][, lab == "3m", drop = FALSE])
  effect <- effect_of(age[keep_cells])
  perms <- sapply(seq_len(n_perm), function(i) abs(effect_of(sample(age[keep_cells]))))

  # Smallest cutoff whose expected false-discovery share is <= target
  cutoff <- NA
  for (t in quantile(abs(effect), seq(0.5, 1, length.out = 200))) {
    n_obs <- sum(abs(effect) > t)
    if (n_obs && (sum(perms > t) / n_perm) / n_obs <= target_fdr) { cutoff <- t; break }
  }
  if (is.na(cutoff)) cutoff <- quantile(apply(perms, 2, max), 0.95)   # family-wise fallback

  hits <- names(effect)[abs(effect) > cutoff]
  if (!length(hits)) return(list(table = NULL, effect = effect))
  present <- intersect(ages, unique(age))
  means <- matrix(sapply(present, function(a) rowMeans(expr[hits, age == a, drop = FALSE])),
                  nrow = length(hits), dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("mean_", present)))
  out <- data.frame(feature = hits, effect = effect[hits], means)
  # Do 9m and 12m sit between the endpoints, in order?
  mid <- intersect(c("mean_9m", "mean_12m"), names(out))
  frac <- sapply(mid, function(m) (out[[m]] - out$mean_3m) / (out$mean_18m - out$mean_3m))
  out$monotonic <- if (length(mid)) apply(matrix(frac, nrow = nrow(out)), 1, function(f)
    all(f >= 0 & f <= 1) && !is.unsorted(f)) else NA
  list(table = out[order(-abs(out$effect)), ], effect = effect)
}

endpoint_genes <- list(); endpoint_adt <- list(); endpoint_gsea <- list()
gobp <- if (packageVersion("msigdbr") >= "10.0.0") {
  msigdbr(species = "Mus musculus", collection = "C5", subcollection = "GO:BP")
} else {
  msigdbr(species = "Mus musculus", category = "C5", subcategory = "GO:BP")
}
gobp <- split(gobp$gene_symbol, gobp$gs_name)

for (st in stages) for (sx in names(sex_cols)) {
  cells <- colnames(gmp_neu)[gmp_neu$stage == st & gmp_neu$sex == sx]
  age <- gmp_neu$age[cells]
  if (sum(age == "3m") < min_cells || sum(age == "18m") < min_cells) next
  label <- paste(st, sx)

  rna <- endpoint_contrast(LayerData(gmp_neu, assay = "RNAmatched", layer = "data")[, cells], age)
  if (!is.null(rna$table)) endpoint_genes[[label]] <- mutate(rna$table, stage = st, sex = sx)
  adt <- endpoint_contrast(LayerData(gmp_neu, assay = "ADT", layer = "data")[, cells], age,
                           min_detected = 0)
  if (!is.null(adt$table)) endpoint_adt[[label]] <- mutate(adt$table, stage = st, sex = sx)

  ranks <- sort(rna$effect, decreasing = TRUE)
  sets <- lapply(gobp, intersect, names(ranks))
  gsea <- fgsea(sets[lengths(sets) >= 15 & lengths(sets) <= 500], ranks)
  top <- gsea[which(gsea$padj < 0.05), ]
  main <- if (nrow(top)) collapsePathways(top, sets, ranks)$mainPathways else character()
  endpoint_gsea[[label]] <- gsea |> filter(pathway %in% main) |>
    mutate(stage = st, sex = sx, leadingEdge = sapply(leadingEdge, paste, collapse = ";"))
}

endpoint_genes <- bind_rows(endpoint_genes)
endpoint_adt <- bind_rows(endpoint_adt)
endpoint_gsea <- bind_rows(endpoint_gsea)
write.csv(endpoint_genes, file.path(out_dir, "endpoint_genes.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(endpoint_adt, file.path(out_dir, "endpoint_adt.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(endpoint_gsea, file.path(out_dir, "endpoint_gsea.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
count(endpoint_genes, stage, sex, monotonic)
```

# 9. NB-GLM models

Per sex: does a gene change with age? Jointly: does it change differently in
the two sexes? The cutoff comes from refitting on shuffled labels, not from BH
on per-cell p-values. **Changed: stage is a covariate**, and age is shuffled
within stage for the null. Without it, the models pooled stages whose mix moves
in opposite directions in the two sexes, and the top "interaction" genes
(Mmp8, Mmp9, Retnlg) were just the stage shift.

```{r}
neus <- subset(gmp_neu, CytoTRACE2_Potency == "Differentiated")
neus$stage <- droplevels(neus$stage)
meta <- neus@meta.data[, c("age", "sex", "stage")]
meta$age <- factor(meta$age, levels = ages)
meta$sex <- factor(meta$sex)
counts <- LayerData(neus, assay = "RNAmatched_sex", layer = "counts")
counts <- counts[rowSums(counts > 0) >= 10, ]

lrt <- function(cts, md, full, reduced)
  test_de(glm_gp(cts, design = full, col_data = md, size_factors = "normed_sum"),
          reduced_design = reduced)
shuffle_age <- function(md) { md$age <- ave(as.character(md$age), md$stage, FUN = sample)
                              md$age <- factor(md$age, levels = ages); md }
shuffle_sex <- function(md) { md$sex <- factor(ave(as.character(md$sex), md$age, md$stage, FUN = sample)); md }

# Largest p-value cutoff whose empirical FDR (from the permuted fits) is <= 5%
calibrate <- function(obs_p, null_p, target = 0.05) {
  grid <- 10^seq(-10, log10(0.05), length.out = 300)
  fdr <- sapply(grid, function(cut) mean(null_p < cut) * length(obs_p) / max(1, sum(obs_p < cut)))
  if (any(fdr <= target)) grid[max(which(fdr <= target))] else 0
}

run_model <- function(cts, md, full, reduced, shuffle) {
  obs <- lrt(cts, md, full, reduced)
  null_p <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(glm_n_perm), function(i) lrt(cts, shuffle(md), full, reduced)$pval))
  cut <- calibrate(obs$pval, null_p)
  obs[obs$pval < cut, ] |> arrange(pval)
}

glm_hits <- list()
for (sx in levels(meta$sex)) {
  i <- meta$sex == sx
  glm_hits[[sx]] <- run_model(counts[, i], droplevels(meta[i, ]), ~ stage + age, ~ stage, shuffle_age)
}
glm_hits$interaction <- run_model(counts, meta, ~ stage + age * sex, ~ stage + age + sex, shuffle_sex)
for (nm in names(glm_hits))
  write.csv(glm_hits[[nm]], file.path(out_dir, paste0("glm_", nm, ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)
sapply(glm_hits, nrow)
```

Along the trajectory: does a gene's developmental profile differ with age, with
sex, or in shape? 3m vs 18m only, on the pseudotime span every group covers
(group-specific splines extrapolate freely outside their own range).

```{r}
cd <- gmp_neu@meta.data |> mutate(cell = colnames(gmp_neu), pt = pseudotime) |>
  filter(is.finite(pt), age %in% c("3m", "18m")) |>
  mutate(age = factor(age, levels = c("3m", "18m")), sex = factor(sex))
span <- cd |> group_by(age, sex) |> summarise(lo = min(pt), hi = max(pt), .groups = "drop")
cd <- filter(cd, pt >= max(span$lo), pt <= min(span$hi))
cts <- LayerData(gmp_neu, assay = "RNAmatched_sex", layer = "counts")[, cd$cell]
cts <- cts[rowSums(cts > 0) >= 10, ]

shuffle_both <- function(md) { i <- sample(nrow(md)); md$age <- md$age[i]; md$sex <- md$sex[i]; md }
f_full   <- ~ splines::ns(pt, 3) * age * sex
traj_any <- run_model(cts, cd, ~ splines::ns(pt, 3) + age * sex + splines::ns(pt, 3):age +
                        splines::ns(pt, 3):sex, ~ splines::ns(pt, 3), shuffle_both)
traj_age <- run_model(cts, cd, f_full, ~ splines::ns(pt, 3) * sex, shuffle_both)
traj_sex <- run_model(cts, cd, f_full, ~ splines::ns(pt, 3) * age, shuffle_both)

traj_any$driver <- with(traj_any, ifelse(name %in% traj_age$name & name %in% traj_sex$name, "both",
                                  ifelse(name %in% traj_age$name, "age",
                                  ifelse(name %in% traj_sex$name, "sex", "joint only"))))
write.csv(traj_any, file.path(out_dir, "trajectory_model_hits.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
table(traj_any$driver)
```

# 10. Sex x age interaction GSEA, per stage

Is a pathway's age trend different between the libraries? Per sex, Spearman rho
of each gene against age; the Fisher-z difference ranks genes; preranked GSEA.
A positive NES means only "the age trend is more positive in males", and each
pathway's leading edge says what the genes actually do. **Changed:** each stage
keeps the ages at which both sexes have enough cells (the original required all
of them, which ruled out mature and immature entirely), it uses `RNAmatched_sex`,
and sex-chromosome genes are left out of the ranking (they top any contrast of
the two libraries and say nothing about granulopoiesis).

```{r}
sex_chr <- c("Xist", "Tsix", "Ddx3y", "Uty", "Eif2s3y", "Kdm5d", "Jpx", "Ftx")
months <- c("3m" = 3, "9m" = 9, "12m" = 12, "18m" = 18)

rho_by_sex <- function(expr, age_months) {
  expr <- expr[rowMeans(expr > 0) >= 0.05, , drop = FALSE]
  # apply() over genes returns cells x genes: one column per gene
  rho <- cor(apply(as.matrix(expr), 1, rank), rank(age_months))[, 1]
  data.frame(gene = rownames(expr), rho = rho, n = ncol(expr))
}

interaction_gsea <- list()
for (st in c("GMPs", "preNeu", "immature", "mature")) {
  in_stage <- gmp_neu$stage == st
  n <- table(factor(gmp_neu$age[in_stage], levels = ages), gmp_neu$sex[in_stage])
  use <- rownames(n)[apply(n >= min_cells, 1, all)]
  if (length(use) < 2) next
  cells <- colnames(gmp_neu)[in_stage & gmp_neu$age %in% use]
  expr <- LayerData(gmp_neu, assay = "RNAmatched_sex", layer = "data")

  r <- lapply(c(male = "male", female = "female"), function(sx) {
    cc <- cells[gmp_neu$sex[cells] == sx]
    rho_by_sex(expr[, cc], months[gmp_neu$age[cc]])
  })
  tab <- inner_join(r$male, r$female, by = "gene", suffix = c("_M", "_F")) |>
    filter(!gene %in% sex_chr, is.finite(rho_M), is.finite(rho_F)) |>
    mutate(z_diff = (atanh(pmin(abs(rho_M), 0.999) * sign(rho_M)) -
                     atanh(pmin(abs(rho_F), 0.999) * sign(rho_F))) /
                    sqrt(1 / (n_M - 3) + 1 / (n_F - 3)))
  ranks <- setNames(tab$z_diff, tab$gene)
  sets <- lapply(gobp, intersect, names(ranks))
  res <- fgsea(sets[lengths(sets) >= 15 & lengths(sets) <= 500], ranks)
  top <- res[which(res$padj < 0.05), ]
  main <- if (nrow(top)) collapsePathways(top, sets, ranks)$mainPathways else character()
  interaction_gsea[[st]] <- res |> filter(pathway %in% main) |>
    mutate(stage = st, ages = paste(use, collapse = ","),
           trend_more_positive_in = ifelse(NES > 0, "male", "female"),
           mean_rho_M = sapply(leadingEdge, function(g) mean(tab$rho_M[tab$gene %in% g])),
           mean_rho_F = sapply(leadingEdge, function(g) mean(tab$rho_F[tab$gene %in% g])),
           leadingEdge = sapply(leadingEdge, paste, collapse = ";"))
}
interaction_gsea <- bind_rows(interaction_gsea)
write.csv(interaction_gsea, file.path(out_dir, "interaction_gsea.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
interaction_gsea |> select(stage, ages, pathway, NES, padj, mean_rho_M, mean_rho_F)
```

# 11. Sex-difference candidates for orthogonal validation

Not a test of sex: sex is the library. A ranked list of gene-set scores that
differ between the libraries, each with the assay that could test it. Three
checks decide what to believe:

* **Direction.** The female library is deeper, so female-high is what the
  confound predicts. Male-high candidates had to overcome it.
* **A within-library null.** The same scores compared between random halves of
  the female library, within the stage: a real difference has to beat that.
* **Depth matching.** The effect on `RNAmatched_sex` should keep its sign on
  unmatched counts.

```{r}
assay_keywords <- list(
  "mitochondrial content" = "OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION|ELECTRON_TRANSPORT|ATP_SYNTHESIS|RESPIRATORY_CHAIN",
  "ROS" = "REACTIVE_OXYGEN|OXIDATIVE_STRESS|RESPIRATORY_BURST",
  "NETs" = "EXTRACELLULAR_TRAP|CHROMATIN_DECONDENSATION",
  "phagocytosis" = "PHAGOCYT|DEFENSE_RESPONSE_TO_BACTERIUM",
  "glucose uptake" = "GLYCOLY|GLUCOSE_IMPORT|HEXOSE",
  "CBC" = "GRANULOCYTE_DIFFERENTIATION|MYELOID_CELL_DIFFERENTIATION|CELL_CYCLE_PHASE_TRANSITION")
candidate_sets <- lapply(assay_keywords, function(k) grep(k, names(gobp), value = TRUE))
assay_of <- setNames(rep(names(candidate_sets), lengths(candidate_sets)), unlist(candidate_sets))
sets <- lapply(gobp[names(assay_of)], intersect, rownames(gmp_neu))
sets <- sets[lengths(sets) >= 15 & lengths(sets) <= 500]

score <- function(obj, assay) {
  s <- AddModuleScore_UCell(obj, features = sets, assay = assay, name = "")
  as.matrix(s@meta.data[, names(sets)])
}
smd <- function(x, g) (mean(x[g == "female"]) - mean(x[g == "male"])) / sd(x)

candidates <- list()
for (st in stages) {
  obj <- subset(gmp_neu, stage == st)
  if (min(table(obj$sex)) < min_cells) next
  matched <- score(obj, "RNAmatched_sex")
  raw <- score(obj, "RNA")
  effect <- apply(matched, 2, smd, g = obj$sex)
  effect_raw <- apply(raw, 2, smd, g = obj$sex)
  ci <- apply(matched, 2, function(x) quantile(replicate(200, {
    i <- sample(length(x), replace = TRUE); smd(x[i], obj$sex[i]) }), c(0.025, 0.975)))

  # Random halves of the female library, same stage: the largest |effect| any
  # set reaches when no sex difference exists
  fem <- matched[obj$sex == "female", , drop = FALSE]
  null_max <- replicate(100, {
    g <- sample(rep(c("female", "male"), length.out = nrow(fem)))
    max(abs(apply(fem, 2, smd, g = g)))
  })

  candidates[[st]] <- data.frame(
    stage = st, gene_set = names(effect), orthogonal_assay = assay_of[names(effect)],
    effect_female_minus_male = effect, ci_low = ci[1, ], ci_high = ci[2, ],
    higher_in = ifelse(effect > 0, "female", "male"),
    against_depth_bias = effect < 0,
    beats_within_library_null = abs(effect) > quantile(null_max, 0.95),
    keeps_sign_unmatched = sign(effect) == sign(effect_raw))
}
candidates <- bind_rows(candidates) |>
  arrange(desc(against_depth_bias & beats_within_library_null & keeps_sign_unmatched),
          desc(beats_within_library_null), desc(abs(effect_female_minus_male)))
write.csv(candidates, file.path(out_dir, "sex_candidates.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
head(filter(candidates, beats_within_library_null), 20)

p <- candidates |> filter(beats_within_library_null) |> slice_head(n = 25) |>
  mutate(label = paste0(tolower(gsub("_", " ", sub("^GOBP_", "", gene_set))), " [", stage, "]")) |>
  ggplot(aes(effect_female_minus_male, reorder(label, -effect_female_minus_male), colour = higher_in)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = ci_low, xmax = ci_high, shape = keeps_sign_unmatched)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = sex_cols) + scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Standardised difference, female - male", y = NULL,
       title = "Sex-difference candidates (beat the within-library null)",
       caption = "Sex is confounded with library. Male-high candidates resist the depth bias.")
p; save_plot(p, "sex_candidates", 11, 8)
```
